name: Alpha Innovations

profile.address: 2020 Union Carbide Drive, Building 6000, South Charleston, WV 25303
profile.reading:
Alpha Federal is the branding Alpha Innovations uses on its own website for what the company calls its Global Data Center, a facility occupying Building 6000 at 2020 Union Carbide Drive in South Charleston, West Virginia. The address places the building inside the West Virginia Regional Technology Park, a research and business campus built on land that once housed Union Carbide's South Charleston Technical Center, one of the largest private chemical research operations in the country through much of the twentieth century. After Union Carbide scaled back its South Charleston research presence, the site was redeveloped into a multi-tenant technology park that today hosts a mix of manufacturing, research, and technology tenants. Alpha Innovations occupying a numbered building on this campus is consistent with that pattern of adaptive reuse.

Alpha Innovations describes itself as a managed IT services provider serving government, education, and commercial clients, offering cybersecurity, cloud, voice, and infrastructure services, and citing a 95 percent client retention rate. The company states that Building 6000 totals 80,000 square feet, a figure it publishes directly on its own site, but it does not publish a power capacity in megawatts, a tier classification, a year the building was brought into service as a data center, or a breakdown of which of its stated HIPAA, SOC, and PCI compliance certifications apply specifically to this South Charleston location versus its operations generally.

Because Alpha Innovations markets primarily to government and institutional clients rather than to the open colocation market, it has less commercial incentive than a wholesale or retail colocation operator to publish granular specifications such as power density, cooling architecture, or redundancy tier, information that colocation customers shopping between providers typically expect to see. The absence of that detail here is therefore unsurprising for a facility built to support a single company's managed services book of business rather than to attract third-party tenants. What is publicly confirmed is the address, the building's role as Alpha's primary data center, and its location on a redeveloped industrial research campus with a long institutional history in the Kanawha Valley's chemical and technology sector, a region now trying to reposition part of its economy around technology and cybersecurity work rather than the heavy chemical manufacturing it was historically known for.

reading:
Alpha Innovations is a West Virginia managed IT services company that also runs a data centre, and it belongs in this registry as an example of a common pattern that rarely gets described. A regional provider builds a facility to serve clients it already has, rather than to lease capacity to strangers. The company was founded in 2000 as a small West Virginia IT services firm, is led by chief executive Dr Douglas Tate and chief financial officer Drew Kesler, and is headquartered at 4003 Outlook Drive in Hurricane, West Virginia. It uses the names Alpha Innovations and Alpha Technologies interchangeably across its own materials, which is worth noting for anyone trying to trace it through older trade coverage.

Its service lines run across managed IT, cloud and backup, networking, cybersecurity, voice over IP and more recently AI consulting. The data centre, branded DC1 and also operating under an Alpha Federal identity for government work, sits at 2020 Union Carbide Drive, Building 6000, in the West Virginia Regional Technology Park in South Charleston. The building's history matters more than most. The technology park is the former Union Carbide research campus, later held by Dow and transferred into state hands to be run as a research and technology park. Building 6000 was Union Carbide's own global computing hub, and Alpha acquired it in 2012, a purchase the company itself describes as the turning point that converted a services business into a cloud and infrastructure one. Trade coverage puts the building at roughly 79,700 square feet.

From DC1 the company sells colocation, cloud hosting, disaster recovery, data centre consolidation and backup alongside help desk, network operations and security operations support, and it markets infrastructure, platform, hardware and disaster recovery on an as a service basis. It states HIPAA, PCI DSS and SOC compliance, with FISMA listed as pending. It publishes federal contracting identifiers, unique entity ID HLRTE8M225B8 and CAGE code 4FNG5, and describes federal work including infrastructure and platform services for the United States Geological Survey, which is consistent with the government and research tenants already on the technology park campus.

What is not published is capacity. Neither Alpha Innovations nor the West Virginia Regional Technology Park states a utility service figure, a critical IT load, a design density or a generator rating for DC1, and no West Virginia Public Service Commission siting case or Kanawha County zoning docket covering the building surfaced in this research, which is expected for an existing industrial building reused rather than a new campus. This registry therefore records no megawatt figure for the site. The company also does not publish its ownership structure. Its clearest recent expansion is outside this registry's West Virginia row and outside South Charleston. In late 2024 it announced the conversion of the former Appalachian Power office building at 1125 Sixth Avenue in Huntington, Cabell County, about 60,000 square feet, a roughly 10 million dollar project described as built to Tier III standards, with construction starting in November 2024 and a first phase targeted for March 2025, anchored to a regional fibre build by Thundercloud that drew more than 2.3 million dollars in state funding.
